21983-the-continental-monthly-vol-4-no-1.creator: Unknown
21983-the-continental-monthly-vol-4-no-1.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. The luminous summary of statistical facts published in the March number of the _Atlantic Monthly_ for 1862, has, in a few pages, conclusively settled the question whether emancipation in the smaller islands of the British West Indies has been a success or a failure.

6742-the-school-for-husbands.title: The School For Husbands
6742-the-school-for-husbands.creator: Unknown
6742-the-school-for-husbands.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. ferent education to the children they bring up. One of them is a dotard, who, after having for sixty years been sullen, grumpy and avaricious, becomes suddenly lively, polite, and prodigal; this Molière had too much common sense to imitate.

arxiv-1811-03508.title: A simple yet effective baseline for non-attributed graph classification
arxiv-1811-03508.creator: Chen Cai, Yusu Wang
arxiv-1811-03508.description: Abstract Graphs are complex objects that do not lend themselves easily to typical learning tasks. Recently, a range of approaches based on graph kernels or graph neural networks have been developed for graph classification and for representation learning on graphs in general.

arxiv-2012-00514.title: Multi-Modal Hybrid Architecture for Pedestrian Action Prediction
arxiv-2012-00514.creator: Amir Rasouli*, Tiffany Yau, Mohsen Rohani, Jun Luo
arxiv-2012-00514.description: Abstract Pedestrian behavior prediction is one of the major challenges for intelligent driving systems in urban environments. Pedestrians often exhibit a wide range of behaviors and adequate interpretations of those depend on various sources of information such as pedestrian appearance, states of other road users, the environment layout, etc.

arxiv-2312-02043.title: The largely linear response of earth’s ice volume to orbital forcing
arxiv-2312-02043.creator: Liam Wheen, Thomas Gernon, Cameron Hall, Jerry Wright, Oscar Benjamin
arxiv-2312-02043.description: Abstract Orbital forcing plays a key role in pacing the glacial-interglacial cycles. However, the mechanistic linkages between the orbital parameters — eccentricity, obliquity, and precession — and global ice volume remain unclear. Here, we investigate the effect of Earth’s orbitally governed incoming solar radiation (that is, insolation) on global ice volume over the past 800,000 years.

arxiv-2401-03483.title: The interplay of common noise and finite pulses on biological neurons
arxiv-2401-03483.creator: Afifurrahman 1∗ , Mohd Hafiz Mohd 2 , Farah Aini Abdullah 3 1 Department of Mathematics, Universitas Islam Negeri Mataram, Mataram 83116, Indonesia 2,3 School of Mathematical Sciences, Universiti Sains Malaysia, 11800 USM, Penang, Malaysia *Email: afif.rahman@uinmataram.ac.id
arxiv-2401-03483.description: Abstract The response of neurons is highly sensitive to the stimulus. The stimulus can be associated with a direct injection in vitro experimentation (e.g., time dependent and independent inputs); or post-synaptic potentials resulting from the interaction of many neurons. A typical incoming stimulus resembles a noise which in principle can be described as a random variable.

arxiv-2404-12026.title: Transport scaling in porous media convection
arxiv-2404-12026.creator: Xiaojue Zhu 1, Yifeng Fu 1, Marco De Paoli 2,3
arxiv-2404-12026.description: Abstract We present a theory to describe the Nusselt number ( 𝑁𝑢 \nus ), corresponding to the heat or mass flux, as a function of the Rayleigh–Darcy number ( 𝑅𝑎 \ra ), the ratio of buoyant driving force over diffusive dissipation, in convective porous media flows.

arxiv-2405-11963.title: A Simulation Tool for V2G Enabled Demand Response Based on Model Predictive Control
arxiv-2405-11963.creator: Cesar Diaz-Londono, Stavros Orfanoudakis, Pedro P. Vergara, Peter Palensky, Fredy Ruiz, Giambattista Gruosso
arxiv-2405-11963.description: Abstract Integrating electric vehicles (EVs) into the power grid can revolutionize energy management strategies, offering both challenges and opportunities for creating a more sustainable and resilient grid. In this context, model predictive control (MPC) emerges as a powerful tool for addressing the complexities of Grid-to-vehicle (G2V) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) enabled demand response management.

arxiv-2503-08386.title: X-Ray Spectral Variability of Thirteen TeV High Energy Peaked Blazars with XMM-Newton
arxiv-2503-08386.creator: P. U. Devanand, Alok C. Gupta, V. Jithesh, Paul J. Wiita, Archana Gupta
arxiv-2503-08386.description: Abstract We present a comprehensive study of the X-ray spectral variability observed in 13 TeV photon emitting high energy peaked BL Lacs (HBLs). These data come from 54 XMM-Newton EPIC-PN pointed observations made during its operational period from June 2001 through July 2023. We performed spectral studies in the energy range 0.

arxiv-2503-12855.title: ViTED : Video Temporal Evidence Distillation
arxiv-2503-12855.creator: Yujie Lu, Yale Song, William Wang, Lorenzo Torresani, Tushar Nagarajan
arxiv-2503-12855.description: Abstract We investigate complex video question answering via chain-of-evidence reasoning — identifying sequences of temporal spans from multiple relevant parts of the video, together with visual evidence within them. Existing models struggle with multi-step reasoning as they uniformly sample a fixed number of frames, which can miss critical evidence distributed nonuniformly throughout the video.

arxiv-2504-06879.title: Machine Learning Approach to Study of Low Energy Alpha-Deuteron Elastic Scattering using Phase Function Method
arxiv-2504-06879.creator: Arushi Sharma, Ayushi Awasthi, Jyoti Sharma, Ishwar Kant, M. R. Ganesh Kumar, O. S. K. S. Sastri
arxiv-2504-06879.description: Abstract The present study focuses on the analysis of elastic scattering in the alpha-deuteron system for low-energy data up to 14 MeV. This system holds particular significance due to its direct connection to the L 6 ​ i {}^{6}Li production reaction, which is an important process in nuclear astrophysics and light nuclei synthesis.

arxiv-2505-11724.title: Semantically-Aware Game Image Quality Assessment
arxiv-2505-11724.creator: Kai Zhu, Vignesh Edithal, Le Zhang, Ilia Blank, Imran Junejo
arxiv-2505-11724.description: Abstract Assessing the visual quality of video game graphics presents unique challenges due to the absence of reference images and the distinct types of distortions, such as aliasing, texture blur, and geometry level of detail (LOD) issues, which differ from those in natural images or user-generated content.

arxiv-2602-08076.title: Interplay of Lorentz Invariance Violation and Earth’s Matter Potential in High-Energy Neutrinos
arxiv-2602-08076.creator: Simon Hilding-Nørkjær, Johann Ioannou-Nikolaides, D. Jason Koskinen, Thomas Stuttard
arxiv-2602-08076.description: Abstract Searches for Lorentz invariance violation (LIV) in the neutrino sector have traditionally focused on non-standard neutrino oscillations induced by LIV in vacuum. In this work, however, we study anisotropic LIV in matter. First, we review vacuum LIV phenomenology, explaining the energy and direction dependence of sidereal modulations for anisotropic coefficients in the Standard Model Extension.

doe-osti-3010875-energy-efficient-large-.description: U.S. Department of Energy technical report. plos-pone-0012178.creator: Heath A. Elrod, Songqing Fan, Susan Muller et al.
plos-pone-0012178.description: PLOS ONE research article. Death receptor 5 (DR5) and caspase-8 are major components in the extrinsic apoptotic pathway. The alterations of the expression of these proteins during the metastasis of head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) and their prognostic impact have not been reported. The present

pmc-10636776.title: Flexible Soft-Printed Polymer Films with Tunable Plasmonic Properties
pmc-10636776.creator: Aleksei Solomonov, Anna Kozell, Alexander B Tesler, Iddo Pinkas, Seth Walensky, Ulyana Shimanovich
pmc-10636776.description: Noble metal nanoparticles (NPs) and particularly gold (Au) have become emerging materials in recent decades due to their exceptional optical properties, such as localized surface plasmons. Although multiple and relatively simple protocols have been developed for AuNP synthesis, the functionalization of solid surfaces composed of soft matter with AuNPs often requires complex and multistep processes.

pmc-10709096.title: Experiences and Perceptions of Post-Stroke Fatigue Among Stroke Survivors in Saudi Arabia: A Qualitative Interview Study
pmc-10709096.creator: Wafa Saeed Alahmari, Kholood Matouq Shalabi, Reem M Basuodan, Ahmed Saad Alhowimel, Mazyad Alotaibi
pmc-10709096.description: PurposePost-stroke fatigue (PSF) is a debilitating condition that negatively impacts the quality of life of stroke survivors. The rehabilitation of stroke survivors is important for their quality of life, and rehabilitation programs that cater to the needs of these patients are required. However, there is very little published information on their needs, especially in the Middle East.

pmc-11491268.title: WFITN Activities for Diversity and Inclusion in Neuroendovascular Treatment
pmc-11491268.creator: Michihiro Tanaka
pmc-11491268.description: n Neurointervention, which connects trainees with seasoned INR practitioners, and the Women’s Observership Grant, which offers financial support for educational experiences, are prime examples of WFITN’s dedication to fostering inclusivity. The following article by Suzuki reports her overseas experience of neurointervention supported by the WFITN Women’s Observership Grant in detail.

pmc-11716893.title: Associations Between Brain Structure and Dual Decline in Gait and Cognition
pmc-11716893.creator: Sadhani Karunarathna, Monique Breslin, Jane E Alty, Richard Beare, Taya Collyer, Velandai K Srikanth, Scott McDonald, Michele L Callisaya
pmc-11716893.description: BackgroundDual decline in gait and cognition is associated with an increased risk of dementia, with combined gait and memory decline exhibiting the strongest association. However, little is known about the underlying brain correlates. Therefore, we aimed to examine the associations between measures of brain structure and dual decline in gait and cognition across several cognitive domains.

pmc-12597011.title: Exposure assessment of Campylobacter in United States broiler processing plants – Part 2: prevalence model
pmc-12597011.creator: Rafael E Rivera, Jinquan Wang, Abhinav Mishra, Harshavardhan Thippareddi, Sanjay Kumar, Manpreet Singh
pmc-12597011.description: Poultry processing plants implement controls to reduce Campylobacter prevalence and mitigate gastrointestinal disease risks. Quantitative microbial risk assessments (QMRA) use exposure assessments to evaluate Campylobacter changes and intervention efficacy in U.S. poultry processing plants. However, exposure assessments for poultry parts and comminuted products, representing higher share of total poultry consumption, have not been done till date.

pmc-12859977.title: Prediction of intraoperative acquired pressure injury in elderly cardiac surgery patients via machine learning: model development with the MIMIC-IV and external validation
pmc-12859977.creator: Yi Cheng, Leqi Li, Jiang Zhang, Jifang Zhou, Lihai Chen, Hongwei Shi, Yun Wang, Wei He, Fan Yang
pmc-12859977.description: BackgroundIntraoperative acquired pressure injury (IAPI) represents a major risk in elderly cardiac surgery patients due to skin fragility and impaired perfusion. Reliable risk prediction is essential for prevention and personalized care.MethodsUsing data from 12,222 patients aged ≥60 years in the MIMIC-IV database, we developed machine learning models with 24 clinically relevant features.

pmc-13193780.title: Data to support the modelling of integrated groundwater-surface water flow in permafrost regions, using the Carcajou Watershed, Northwest Territories, Canada
pmc-13193780.creator: Melissa I. Bunn, Omar Khader, Eric Kessel, Steven K. Frey, Andre R. Erler, Hazen A. Russell
pmc-13193780.description: > 50 % of Canada's landmass is underlain by perennially frozen ground (permafrost). These permafrost regions are changing rapidly in response to a warming climate, with Canada’s arctic warming at a rate > 3 times higher than global average. As permafrost distribution shifts in response to this warming, it alters the water cycle, affecting both water quantity and water quality.

pmc-13245467.title: Lipoprotein(a) in Residual Cardiovascular Risk: Measurement Challenges, Assay Standardisation, and Clinical Implications
pmc-13245467.creator: Yiwen Lu, Dongyang Jiang, Jinfeng Zhang, Ying Liang
pmc-13245467.description: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a largely genetically determined, independent contributor to residual atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk, but its clinical interpretation is constrained by measurement complexity. Variation in apolipoprotein(a) [apo(a)] KIV2 copy number, glycosylation, lipid composition, and isoform co-expression complicates mass-based reporting and may cause isoform-sensitive bias in immunoassays.

pmc-13289470.title: Single-model deep learning approach for simultaneous cervical vertebral maturation staging and skeletal jaw relationship on lateral cephalograms using YOLOv8 and CNN
pmc-13289470.creator: Naif Munawir Alotaibi, Ahmed Mohamed Kamel, Abeer Twakol Khalil, Shaza Mohammad Hammad

pmc-13507349.title: Insights from the LysoNeo prospective cohort study to improve newborn screening of lysosomal diseases
pmc-13507349.creator: Abdellah Tebani, David Guenet, Stéphanie Torre, Alina Arion, Bénédicte Héron, Anais Brassier, Nadia Belmatoug, Jérôme Ausseil, Henri Bruel, Catherine Lévéque, Alice Goldenberg, Nicolas Gruchy, Andreea Apetrei, Nathalie Bach, Anne-Marie Guerrot, Simon Samaan, Franklin Ducatez, Stéphane Marret, Soumey
pmc-13507349.description: BackgroundNewborn screening enables early detection and treatment of serious genetic conditions before symptom onset. Lysosomal diseases, a group of more than 70 rare inherited metabolic disorders, are increasingly considered for inclusion in NBS owing to advances in pathophysiological understanding and therapy development. Early, pre-symptomatic identification offers a critical window for intervention that can improve neurodevelopmental outcomes and quality of life.

pmc-13682682.title: Why Police Pull Back? Organizational Injustice and Depolicing
pmc-13682682.creator: Gabriel Béliveau, Massimiliano Mulone, Maude Pérusse-Roy
pmc-13682682.description: Depolicing refers to a perceived decline in police engagement, particularly in proactive enforcement. Although widely invoked in political and media debates, the concept remains theoretically and empirically contested. Existing research suggests that overall police activity remains relatively stable and that only a minority of officers report reducing their own interventions, raising questions about the origins of disengagement narratives.
